A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, The Serial Scaling Hypothesis, with 31 readable pages including Appendices A–G. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–31 are identical; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v3 reports theoretical contributions and illustrative examples, with empirical results in Figures 6–7 explicitly attributed to prior studies. Section 6 states that no new data or code supports the paper. The appendices contain no original empirical study.

after.justification: v4 retains the same externally attributed empirical evidence and unchanged reproducibility statement. Appendices A–G remain identical; the DO1 constructions in Appendix G are theoretical proof devices, not conducted experiments.

M1.justification: The model descriptions, inference procedures, and theoretical constructions are identical. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or method component changes.

E1.justification: The same cellular-automaton, physical-system, RL, and QA examples and externally sourced benchmark evidence remain. No training or evaluation dataset, task, or scenario is added or revised.

E2.justification: Figures 6–7 retain identical MCTS, network-depth-versus-width, and reasoning-chain-versus-majority-vote comparisons. No comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: The settings, budgets, metrics, and procedures described for the cited empirical comparisons are identical. Neither version introduces an original evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added or revised. The supporting examples and analyses throughout the main text and appendices are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the uncertainty displays in Figure 6. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or changed.

E6.justification: Figures 6–7 preserve all plotted results and trends. Numerical diffusion examples in Section 4 and qualitative findings throughout the paper are also unchanged.

T1.justification: All mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs are identical, including the diffusion results in Appendix F and the decision-problem constructions and proofs in Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same Serial Scaling Hypothesis, diffusion-capacity claim, and sequential-decision contributions. The added website line introduces no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including worst-case versus practical seriality and restrictions on the diffusion theorem concerning output dimension and score-modeling accuracy.

D1.justification: v4 adds serial-scaling-hypothesis.github.io below the abstract, providing a new project-site access pointer. The PDFs do not establish that code or data became available; technical documentation and Section 6 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.5, the bibliography, and positioning relative to prior research are identical. No cited research work is added or removed.

P1.justification: Front matter gains a website line, and the arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 14 February 2026 to v4 dated 28 April 2026. Prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The centered website line slightly changes first-page spacing and shifts the introduction and Figure 1. Figure and table contents are unchanged, and rendered pages 2–31 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a project-site pointer and makes minor first-page presentation changes. The scientific argument, evidence, proofs, limitations, and technical documentation remain identical, with no material readability change. The supplied PDFs therefore establish no meaningful overall quality difference.
